title: JavaScript Events Applied Check
description: Test your ability to choose event patterns, debug event targets, handle forms, use delegation, manage async handlers, and prevent performance or cleanup issues.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt:
What is wrong here?
```js
button.addEventListener("click", saveUser());
```

options.text: `saveUser()` runs immediately; pass `saveUser` as the function reference instead
The handler must always be async

questions.explanation: The second argument should be a function reference. Calling `saveUser()` invokes it immediately and passes its return value.

questions.prompt: A button contains an icon span. The listener is on the button. Which property should you use to reliably refer to the button inside that listener?
questions.explanation: `currentTarget` is the element whose listener is currently running. `target` could be the nested span.

questions.prompt: Which delegated click handler best handles clicks on icons inside delete buttons?
questions.explanation: `closest` can find the delete button even when the original target is a nested icon or span.

questions.prompt: A form should be submitted with `fetch` without reloading the page. Which pattern is best?

options.text: Listen for `submit` on the form and call `event.preventDefault()` before the fetch request
Listen for `click` on the document and remove the form
Use `passive: true` and call `preventDefault()` inside it

questions.explanation: The form's `submit` event captures normal submission paths. `preventDefault()` stops the browser navigation so JavaScript can handle the request.

questions.prompt: A search input sends an API request on every `input` event and feels too noisy. Which pattern is usually best?

options.text: Debounce the search handler so it runs after the user pauses typing

questions.explanation: Debouncing is a good fit for search because it waits until rapid input activity pauses.

questions.prompt: A scroll progress indicator needs to update during scrolling without running too often. Which pattern is usually best?

options.text: Throttle the scroll handler and consider a passive listener
Run a large loop inside every `scroll` event

questions.explanation: Throttling limits work during frequent events. `passive: true` can help scrolling stay smooth when default behavior is not prevented.

questions.prompt: A modal adds a `keydown` listener to `document` for Escape. What should happen when the modal closes?

options.text: Remove the listener or abort it with an `AbortController`
Leave the listener forever because the browser deletes all document listeners automatically
Call `preventDefault()` on the close button only

questions.explanation: Long-lived document listeners should be cleaned up when the UI that needed them is removed.

options.text: The listener is not removed because the two arrow functions are different function objects
The listener runs during capture by default

questions.explanation: `removeEventListener` needs the same function reference that was passed to `addEventListener`.

questions.prompt: A parent delegated click listener stopped working after a child button handler was changed. Which child code is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Delegated parent listeners rely on bubbling. `stopPropagation()` can prevent the event from reaching them.

questions.prompt: Which approach is most accessible for an action the user can activate?

options.text: Use a real `<button>` and listen for `click`
Use a `<div>` with only a `mouseenter` listener
Use text that changes only on hover
Disable keyboard focus for the control

questions.explanation: A real button provides expected semantics and keyboard activation, while a click listener handles activation behavior.

questions.prompt: What should an async click handler usually include when a network request can fail?
questions.explanation: Async handlers should handle rejected Promises or thrown errors with `try` / `catch` so the UI can recover.

questions.prompt: A custom `cart:updated` event should let listeners read the new item count. Which event creation is best?
questions.explanation: `CustomEvent` supports a `detail` object for application-specific event data.

questions.prompt: You are debugging why a click listener on a parent reacts to unexpected child clicks. What is a useful first log?
questions.explanation: `target`, `currentTarget`, and the composed path reveal where the event started and how it reached the listener.

questions.prompt: Which event is best for live character counting as the user types in a textarea?
questions.explanation: `input` fires when the value changes, making it a good fit for live character counters.

questions.prompt: A listener is added with `{ capture: true }`. Which removal is correct?
questions.explanation: When removing capture listeners, the event type, function reference, and capture setting must match.
